title: Prefixes and Suffixes (KS2)
subject: English
strapline: Adding beginnings and endings to change what words mean.
facts: A prefix is added to the start of a word to change its meaning: un-, dis-, re-, pre-, mis-, anti-, super-.
un- and dis- often make an opposite: happy → unhappy, agree → disagree.
re- often means again: do → redo, build → rebuild.
A suffix is added to the end of a word: -ed, -ing, -ly, -ful, -less, -ment, -ness, -tion.
Some suffixes change the word class: quick (adjective) → quickly (adverb); enjoy (verb) → enjoyment (noun).
Sometimes the root spelling changes: happy → happiness (y becomes i).

quick_quiz.q: Add a prefix to make the opposite of "kind".
What does the suffix -less mean in "careless"?
Turn "sad" into a noun with a suffix.

teacher_tips: Build words from a root outward so meaning is constructed, not memorised.
Point out spelling changes (y→i, double letters) as you go.
Link prefixes/suffixes to reading — decoding long words gets easier.
